JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,00,000/- for the death of Madhusudan in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner' case are as under:
2. That on 31.01.2021 at about 15.50 a.m. deceased Madhusudan. was traveling in a Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MV-4581 towards Kannur to Kannur Belahalli main road, when he reached near Ragha apartment, at that time, driver of Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 01-AK-8626 drove the same in a negligent manner and suddenly took turn without observing the vehicle coming from behind and without taking any precautions and giving any indications, the deceased who was coming behind the said vehicle, could not control his car and dashed to the Lorry.
Due to which, deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at Dr.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years, doing business and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing registration No.KA-01- AK-8626.
In this regard, Chikkajala Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.17/2021.
As such, the respondents No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
this petition.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before this court,
remained absent, placed exparte.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Concrete Mixer Lorry and liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581, who drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without driving licence, without wearing seat belt and also under influence of Alcohol and himself dashed to the Cement Mixer Lorry bearing registration No. KA-01-AK-8628.
The jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the Lorry only because there was no insurance policy coverage.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioner.

Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive,
exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, her son Madhusudan S/o Manjunath was died in the road traffic accident which occurred on 31.01.2021 at about 12.50 a.m., in front of Raga Apartment, Kannuru-Belahalli Main Road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3) What order or award?

8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.2 examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P23.
9.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has examined Manager of the respondent No.2 company as RW1 and got marked document as Ex.R1.
Further examined its Legal Manager as RW2.
10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

11. My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
Manjunath.

sentences.text:
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01- AK-8626, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently Madhusudan, died at the spot.
13.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 have contended in its written statement that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581.
14.
On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against both the vehicles in question.
On the other hand, onus shifts on the respondents to prove the same by means of cogent and convincing evidence.
15. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 himself examined as PW1.
In his examination- in-chief by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioners in support of their oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
Ex. P1-true copy of the FIR, Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5- true copy of Inquest, Ex.P6-true copy of PM report, Ex.P7-true copy of IMV report,
Ex.P8-true copy of charge sheet.

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Channegowda, son of the deceased, the S.H.O. of Chickjala Traffic Police have registered the case against the drivers of both the vehicles for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet alleging that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and driver of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 have committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
17.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 examined Manager of respondent No.2 company as RW1.
He has placed authorisation letter.
18. Further examined Legal Manager as RW2.

He has deposed in his evidence that the deceased who was driving his car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 in a rash and negligent manner without driving licence without wearing seat belt and also under the influence of alcohol himself dashed to Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 and falsely implicated the respondent No.2 vehicle.

19. On going through the Ex.P1 first information report reveals that, on the basis of first information statement at Ex.P2 given by Channegowda alleging that, driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and driver of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 have committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
20.

Added to this, on perusal of the spot mahazar Ex.P3 and its recitals executed in the presence of panch witnesses and narration made in the Ex.P4 spot sketch clearly indicate about the involvement of both the vehicles in the accident.

The direction of both the vehicles shown in the spot sketch,
discloses that, there was negligence on the part of the drivers of both the vehicles to cause accident.

sentences.text: Even on going through the damages noted in the Ex.P5-IMV report discloses about the negligence on the part of the drivers of both the vehicles.
All these material documents remained unquestioned and unshaken by placing the contra materials.

21. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer evident that,
said report has been filed against drivers of both the vehicles by name Madhusudan, the driver of the voksvagen car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581, who is none other than the deceased in this case and Ali Ahamed, driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 alleging that, they have committed the offences punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC and Section 134(a & b) R/W section 187 and 185 of MV Act.
As such, both the drivers are responsible for the accident.

22. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, though several questions put to him,
the PW1 had denied that, due to his negligence accident in question had taken place.
Even the respondent No.1 company also, not made an effort to prove the innocence of the driver of the vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626.
Hence, the charge sheet in the case on hand, is not the conclusive proof.
At the most, that may be a circumstance which has to be considered along with other materials on record.

To disprove the charge sheet contents, no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P8.
23.

In the light of the above discussions, I am of the view that the alleged accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MV-4581 and KA- 01-AK-8628.
Accordingly, issue No.1 in both the cases is answered partly in Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 :
24.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioner, to prove the relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P9 & Ex.P10 i.e., aadhar card of the petitioners have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

25. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioner, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioners are the parents of deceased, in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care of their son, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioner.
By taking into consideration of all these factors along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners are the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.

sentences.text: The petitioners herein, have placed Pass port at Ex.P11 and D.L. at Ex.P13 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 14.5.1995.
The accident occurred on 31.01.2021.

Therefore,
as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 26 years.

For his age, multiplier '17' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
27.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing business and earning Rs.1,50,000/-
per month.

In this regard the petitioners have placed income tax returns for the assessment year 2020-2021, IT returns 2018-2019, D.L., Registration certificate (GST), invoice, voucher remittance, vehicle loan, pass book, B register extract, vehicle network agreement, D.L. and bank statement at Ex.P12 to Ex.P23.
On perusal of the said documents, it does not show the exact income of the deceased per month.

Hence,
considering the nature of the business, if Rs.30,000/- is considered the income of the deceased per month, it will meet the ends of justice.

28. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
29. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income,
an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

"
30. Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor, deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 26 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the Manjunath.

6 deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein as on the date of the accident, was not having permanent job.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.30,000/- per month. And Rs.3,60,000/- per year.

Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased,
comes to (Rs.3,60,000+1,44,000)= Rs.5,04,000/-, and 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus net loss income comes to Rs.2,52,000/-
(Rs.5,04,000- Rs.2,52,000).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "17".

In toto it comes to Rs.42,84,000/- .
31.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

32. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- is awarded to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
33.

(Rupees forty four lakhs five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016,

LIABILITY:-
35.

As regards the liability is concerned, as already discussed in issue No.1 that, the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and driver of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626.

Therefore,
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
36. Further as per the records insurance policy of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 was valid from 15.5.2020 to 14.5.2021.
The alleged accident had taken place on 31.1.2021.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy of the concrete mixer Lorry, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation at the ratio of 50% with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization and remaining 50% contributory negligence is fixed on the deceased.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
37.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,05,000/-
(Rupees forty four lakhs five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners at the ratio of 50% with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order and remaining 50% contributory negligence is fixed on the deceased.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.
Out of the compensation amount together with interest, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Manjunath.
